newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks close higher in mild rebound.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks close higher in mild rebound.

text.p: Taiwan share prices see-sawed through Wednesday's session to finish slightly higher in what brokers called a mild technical rebound, but brokers said the market still lacked upward momentum.
The weighted index closed 26.14 points or 0.33 percent higher at 8,022.89. Turnover was T$67 billion.
Some brokers noted that government-related funds appeared to have entered and bought up carefully targeted shares to prevent a downward correction, but general sentiment remained sluggish.
"Individual investors are still very cautious," Nomura Securities' analyst Amy Huang said.
Electronics, which had suffered from strong profit-taking in the market's May correction, rebounded 2.08 percent, with Taiwan Semiconductor rising T$4 or 3.96 percent to T$105.
The market gave a tepid welcome to the government's plan to commission private fund management firms to manage some T$350 billion worth of state funds by the end of December.

An official at the cabinet's Council for Economic Planning and Development said the move would help to promote Taiwan's aim of becoming a regional asset-management centre and to increase institutional investors' investment ratios in the stock and bond markets.
"It (private management is good news from a longer term point of view, but will have no immediate impact on the market," said Tsao Chung-ping, an analyst of Ting Kong Securiteis.
Investor paid little attention to the governmetn's morning announcement of healthy year-on-year rises for Taiwan's April export orders and industrial output, brokers said.
"Investors rarely react to those figures, unless they are extremely dramatic," Nomura's Huang said.
Foreign orders for Taiwan goods rose a year-on-year 5.91 percent to US$10.490 billion in April, the second-highest value on record, while industrial output rose an annual 6.12 percent.
